addressForm: आप with polite -ें/-एँ imperatives (करें, चुनें, शुरू करें). DineOpen’s Hindi blog (dineopen.com/hi) writes “बेस्ट बिलिंग सॉफ्टवेयर कैसे चुनें”, “free plan के साथ शुरू करें”; Zomato’s Hindi app (launched Nov 2022) and Indian vendor copy use आप. Never तुम/तू. Vendor blogs mix in Latin-script English (Hinglish: “Online orders लेते हैं?”, “7 दिन का free trial”); HatchGrab pages should keep the loanwords but write them in Devanagari.

sources: https://www.dineopen.com/hi/blog/restaurant-billing-software-guide-2026 — Indian vendor’s Hindi blog: आप + -ें imperatives (“कैसे चुनें”, “शुरू करें”), nukta used (ज़रूरी, फ़र्क), ASCII digits and ₹ (“₹899/month”), “बिलिंग सॉफ्टवेयर”, “QR मेनू”; heavy Hinglish (order, KOT, POS, UPI, free trial left in Latin script)

WebSearch “रेस्टोरेंट बिलिंग सॉफ्टवेयर POS ऑनलाइन ऑर्डर टेकअवे KOT” — Indian market calls the till “billing software”/POS (Petpooja “Restaurant Billing Software”, Gofrugal, PosBytz, BharatERP BHOQ “टेकअवे बिलिंग”); KOT and KDS are standard terms; UPI, card, cash, wallet
WebSearch “Zomato Hindi app …” — Zomato launched its app in Hindi in Nov 2022 (Inc42, Business Standard, India TV); Zomato offers a restaurant pickup option (The News Minute)
WebSearch “फूड ट्रक बिजनेस कैसे शुरू करें” — Tata Capital’s Hindi blog ranks for the Devanagari how-to query (page itself returned HTTP 406)

WebSearch “"फ़ूड ट्रक" स्ट्रीट फ़ूड फेस्टिवल दिल्ली” — all results English-language Indian press (Delhi Food Truck Festival, Delhi food-truck policy, 16 locations): the Indian food-truck scene is written about in English

WebSearch “Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020 …” — Rule 4(9): consent to purchase only by an explicit and affirmative action, no pre-ticked boxes (Trilegal, Mondaq, IndiaLaw); no prescribed button wording
confidence: Med-Low — address form, nukta use, POS/billing-software, KOT/KDS, UPI and the order-button rule are confirmed on Indian vendor/legal sources; the Devanagari spellings of टेकअवे, पिकअप का समय, प्री-ऑर्डर, the Pay at Hatch wording and plan names rest on observed Hinglish patterns, not on a fetched Swiggy/Zomato Hindi screen. No search-volume tool: Indian food-truck and software searches are overwhelmingly in English or romanised Hindi (every result for the Devanagari query was English); Devanagari searches appear mainly for how-to topics. csvRows are what the research tool (US-indexed WebSearch) returned for “फ़ूड ट्रक ऑनलाइन ऑर्डर सिस्टम सॉफ्टवेयर”, not local Google ranks.
decisions: Nukta: recommend फ़ूड ट्रक (with nukta, as DineOpen and standard modern Hindi print write ज़/फ़) on pages; searchers often type फूड ट्रक without nukta — Google usually folds the two, but a native/Keyword Planner check is worth doing before launch.

Search language: Indian buyers mostly search in English (“food truck POS”, “online ordering system for food truck”). Consider keeping the en-IN/English page as the main SEO page for India and treating hi-IN as a conversion page; or add the English term in brackets in a few headings.

Pay at Hatch: “पिकअप के समय भुगतान” (feature) / “पिकअप पर भुगतान” (label). Avoid “कैश ऑन डिलीवरी”/“COD” (there is no delivery) and avoid implying cash only — at the truck customers pay by UPI, card or cash.
Takeaway word: Indians say both टेकअवे and पार्सल; recommend टेकअवे in UI with पार्सल as a secondary keyword.

Order button: India has no statutory button wording (Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020, Rule 4(9) only requires explicit, affirmative consent, no pre-ticked boxes). Recommend “ऑर्डर करें” / “ऑर्डर कन्फ़र्म करें”.
